# Rask

> Rask is the .NET One Person Framework: one developer builds, runs, and ships a whole product — UI,
> data, auth, background work, deployment — from a single C# codebase on one server, with SQLite as the
> production database (no PaaS, no assembled service stack, no second language). The UI is plain C#
> components (a Roslyn factory generator, scoped CSS/JS, routing) whose same code runs server-rendered
> over WebSockets, client-side on WebAssembly, or native iOS/Android (Rask.Native); markup uses generated
> factory methods + a children indexer (`Div()[Span(), "hi"]`). Batteries: the `rask` CLI, a
> `generate feature` CQRS+EF CRUD scaffolder, Rask.Cqrs, Rask.Data, production SQLite (pragmas + backup),
> auth, and `--docker` deploy.

This file helps AI coding assistants build apps with Rask. Start with the repo-root AGENTS.md
(the AI guidance shipped alongside this file) for app-authoring conventions, then the docs below.

## Docs
- [The .NET One Person Framework](docs/one-person-framework.md): the doctrine — one dev, whole product, one C# codebase on one server, SQLite-first; links the batteries + roadmap.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, first app, project layout.
- [The `rask` CLI](docs/cli.md): the optional `Rask.Cli` .NET tool (`dotnet tool install -g Rask.Cli`) — a thin, dependency-free wrapper over the SDK. `rask new <name> [--template server|wasm|wasm-hosted|native] [--auth] [--pwa] [--cqrs] [--docker] [--output]` generates the project directly (the CLI owns all scaffolding — no `dotnet new`, no separate templates package), forwarding only the flags that template supports (fails fast otherwise); server is the default template, wasm-hosted emits a three-project `<Name>.Client` (browser-WASM SPA) + `<Name>.Server` (ASP.NET host you run/deploy) + `<Name>.Shared` (class library) solution, `--output` overrides the target directory; `rask generate <page|component|feature> <Name>` (aliases `rask g`, `g f`/`g c`/`g p`) scaffolds a routed page (`Features/<Name>/<Name>Page.cs`), a component (`Components/<Name>.cs`), or a full **CQRS + EF Core CRUD `feature`** under `Features/<Plural>/`: an encapsulated entity (private setters + static `Create`/`Update`; Guid id by default, `--id int|long`), a `DbContext` (or `--context` existing), create/update/delete commands + list/get queries each with a handler that owns the EF access (create/update carry a request object the form binds to), and list/create/edit pages that dispatch via `IDispatcher` with type-safe `Routes.*()` nav. Fields are **positional** — `rask g f Product Name:string Price:decimal` (legacy `--fields "n:type,…"` still accepted, not both); types string/int/long/decimal/double/bool/date/time/datetime/Guid(+aliases), optional with trailing `?`, string max-length via `(N)` (default 200), Id auto-added; `--plural`/`--output`/`--force`/`--dry-run`; prints `AddRaskCqrs()`+`AddDbContextFactory`+`dotnet ef` next-steps. Finds the owning .csproj, derives the folder-based namespace, won't overwrite without `--force`, output compiles as-is; `rask db <add|remove|list|update|drop> [<name>] [--project/-p] [--startup-project/-s] [--context/-c] [--output/-o] [--force/-f] [-- ef args]` wraps `dotnet ef` for the migration lifecycle (add/remove/list migrations, update/drop the database), resolving the project from the single .csproj at/above the CWD and installing `dotnet-ef` globally on first use if missing; `rask dev [--project] [--no-hot-reload] [-- app args]` runs `dotnet watch run`; `rask deploy [--host user@box] [--domain app.example.com] [--port] [--name] [--project] [--dockerfile] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--env-file] [--dry-run]` builds+runs the app on a single host over SSH (every op is `docker -H ssh://host …` — no registry/local daemon; builds on the box), remembering host/domain in `.rask/deploy.json` (never secrets); `--domain` fronts it with a shared auto-HTTPS Caddy proxy (Let's Encrypt) and deploys are zero-downtime blue-green with multiple apps sharing one box (routing regenerated from each container's `rask.*` labels), no `--domain` publishes `--port` (default 8080) for your own proxy; `rask info` reports CLI/SDK/OS; `rask --version`.
- [Live playground](docs/playground.md): write Rask component C# in the browser with a real IDE and see it compile + render live — Roslyn + the Rask source generator run entirely in WebAssembly (no server), the emitted component is Assembly.Load-ed and mounted as a child of the playground's own tree so its handlers/state run through the shared live session. The editor has Roslyn `CompletionService` IntelliSense and as-you-type diagnostics (CS + RASK) as inline Monaco squiggles, driven by a workspace-backed analysis path that never Emits/loads (so typing can't leak assemblies — only Run does); a left-hand gallery offers Counter / Form+validation / Todo starters (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs). The `samples/Rask.Example.Playground` app, published to GitHub Pages at `/rask/playground/` next to the showcase; ships untrimmed (Roslyn reads the `_framework/*.dll` back as metadata references, so WasmEnableWebcil=false; Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features adds CompletionService), user code always runs interpreted, entry point is a `Playground : Component` in a namespace.
- [Best practices](docs/best-practices.md): production patterns + common pitfalls across components, state, forms, data, security, accessibility, performance, testing (each links the deep dive).
- [Elements & the DSL](docs/elements.md): the render surface — the primitives (`Text` HTML-encodes, `Raw` is verbatim, `Doctype`) and the `[...]` collection expression for sibling fragments; a generator-emitted factory for every HTML and SVG element; the universal props (`Id`/`Class`/`Style`/`Data`/`Role`/`TabIndex`/`Aria`, fixed attribute render order) on every tag; typed SVG components (no `Raw()`); and the full HTML-element catalog by category.
- [Routing](docs/routing.md): `[Route]`, params, `Router()`/`Outlet()`, navigation.
- [Lifecycle](docs/lifecycle.md): OnMount/OnPropsChanged/OnRendered/OnUnmount, async hooks.
- [Composition](docs/composition.md): the three component tiers (static method vs stateless vs stateful component), children, context (provide/consume), callbacks, toast messages (Rails-style `IToaster` — scoped-per-session, consumed-once transient messages that survive a client-side navigation; drained by a headless `ToastOutlet`, or `Rask.Bootstrap`'s ready-made `BsToaster`), the full DOM `GlobalEventHandlers` event surface on every element (mouse/pointer/touch/wheel/focus/keyboard/clipboard/drag as typed `OnX`+`OnXAsync` pairs; Audio/Video add the `HTMLMediaElement` events), headless primitives (`VirtualizeModel<T>`), drag-and-drop.
- [Forms](docs/forms.md): binding, validation, EditContext, building form components — implement `IFormControl<T>` (Rask.Core.Forms) on a generic component and the generator synthesizes its controlled + bound factories, or use the public binding API directly (`ExpressionAccessor`/`BindingHelpers`/`RegisterFieldValidator`). `IFormControl<T>` is the framework primitive; ready-made `BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`/`BsMultiSelect` typed controls now ship in the optional Rask.Bootstrap package (the samples keep copyable build-your-own versions). The Bootstrap form controls (`BsInput`/`BsTextarea`/`BsSelect`/`BsCheck`) auto-wire `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` + a `role="alert"` error region when a bound field is invalid.
- [Bootstrap (Rask.Bootstrap)](docs/bootstrap.md): optional package of typed Bootstrap 5.3 component factories (`BsButton`/`BsCard`/`BsModal`/…), zero-JS interactive components driven by the live runtime (`BsModal`/`BsOffcanvas` incl. responsive drawer/`BsAccordion`/`BsTabs`/`BsDropdown`/`BsToast`, controlled state), SPA-routed navigation (`BsNavbar`/`BsNav`/`BsNavItem`, auto-active via `NavLink`), `IFormControl<T>`-bound inputs (`BsInput`/`BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`, and the data-driven combobox `BsSelect`/`BsMultiSelect` — a `.form-select` display box opening a `.dropdown-menu` listbox, with an opt-in `Filter` predicate `(item,text)=>bool` that adds a search field IN the dropdown, nullable × clear, float-when-filled label, `Native: true` for the OS `<select>`, plus hand-editable custom-popover `BsDatePicker`/`BsTimePicker`/`BsDateTimePicker` calendar/clock controls — type the value (live culture parse) or pick, zero-JS, keyboard-navigable, localized, Min/Max/Disable, optional seconds, native fallback), color modes (`BsTheme`), a typed `BsIcon`, and typed utility classes (`Bs.Join(Shadow.Sm, Margin.Bottom(4, Bp.Md))`); bundles Bootstrap 5.3.8 + Bootstrap Icons 1.13.1 as static assets, linked with `BootstrapStyles()`. The guide is one small page per component group (below); this hub page covers setup, color modes, the typed enums, the component map, and versioning.
- [Bootstrap buttons & badges](docs/bootstrap-buttons.md): `BsButton`/`BsButtonGroup`/`BsBadge`/`BsCloseButton` with typed `BsColor`/`BsSize` variants.
- [Bootstrap cards, lists & tables](docs/bootstrap-cards.md): `BsCard` (+`BsCardHeader/Body/Footer/Title/Subtitle/Text/Image`), `BsListGroup`, `BsPlaceholder`, `BsTable`, `BsPagination`, `BsBreadcrumb`.
- [Data grid](docs/data-grid.md): `BsDataGrid<T>` + `BsColumn<T>` — typed columns bound to the row type, click-to-sort headers (`Sortable`/`SortKey`), client-side paging (`PageSize`), footer totals computed over every row (`Footer`/`FooterTemplate`), custom cells (`Template`), an `Empty` placeholder, and master-detail rows (`ExpandedContent`, needs `RowKey`). Zero JS; sorts/pages in memory, so page in the query for large sets.
- [Bootstrap alerts, spinners & progress](docs/bootstrap-feedback.md): dismissible `BsAlert` (controlled close), `BsSpinner`, `BsProgress`.
- [Bootstrap icons](docs/bootstrap-icons.md): the typed `BsIcon` over every Bootstrap Icons glyph via the generated `BsIconName` enum.
- [Bootstrap navbar & nav](docs/bootstrap-navigation.md): `BsNavbar`/`BsNavbarBrand`/`BsNav`/`BsNavItem` — SPA-routed, auto-active via `NavLink`, zero-JS.
- [Bootstrap modals, offcanvas & dropdowns](docs/bootstrap-overlays.md): controlled, zero-JS `BsModal` (focus-trapped, Escape-closes)/`BsOffcanvas` (responsive drawer)/`BsDropdown`; all `.dropdown-menu` popovers are re-anchored `position:fixed` while open (opt-in `data-rask-popover`) to escape overflow-clipping ancestors (plus `BsPopover`/`BsConfirmDialog`).
- [Bootstrap tabs, accordion & collapse](docs/bootstrap-disclosure.md): controlled, zero-JS `BsTabs`/`BsAccordion`/`BsCollapse`.
- [Bootstrap toasts](docs/bootstrap-toasts.md): controlled `BsToast` (stacked, auto-hidden from Rask state) and the `BsToaster` outlet that drains `IToaster` messages.
- [Bootstrap form controls](docs/bootstrap-forms.md): the `IFormControl<T>`-bound `BsInput`/`BsTextarea`/`BsCheck`/`BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup` + layout helpers (`BsFormGroup`/`BsFormLabel`/`BsInputGroup`); auto-wire `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` + a `role="alert"` error region when invalid.
- [Bootstrap selects & multiselect](docs/bootstrap-select.md): the data-driven combobox `BsSelect`/`BsMultiSelect` — a `.form-select` display box opening a `.dropdown-menu` listbox, opt-in `Filter` search field, nullable × clear, float-when-filled label, `Native` OS `<select>`; full roving-cursor keyboard model over the flat option list with `aria-activedescendant`/`role=option` (multiselect listbox is `aria-multiselectable`, Enter/Space toggle membership), opening focuses the filter and Enter/Esc/arrows stay inside the dropdown (single-select Enter picks without submitting the form), `OptionValue` projected-id binding, `OptionGroup` grouping (`<optgroup>` / `.dropdown-header`), `OptionDisabled` per-option disable (cursor skips it), and a multiselect `SelectAll` "Select all / Clear all" header.
- [Bootstrap date & time pickers](docs/bootstrap-pickers.md): hand-editable custom-popover `BsDatePicker`/`BsTimePicker`/`BsDateTimePicker` calendar/clock controls — type the value (live culture parse) or pick, zero-JS, full keyboard nav (arrows/Page/Home/End/Enter), localized, Min/Max/Disable, optional seconds column, `Labels` to translate the chrome, nullable × clear, native fallback.
- [Bootstrap utility classes](docs/bootstrap-utilities.md): typed utility-class tokens (`Shadow`/`Border`/`Margin`/`Padding`/`Display`/`Flex`/`Rounded`/`Txt`/`Font`/`Sizing`/`Position`/`Bg`) composed with `Bs.Join(Shadow.Sm, Margin.Bottom(4, Bp.Md))`, with an optional responsive `Bp` infix.
- [Building form controls](docs/building-form-controls.md): end-to-end guide to authoring a custom control with `IFormControl<T>` — the interface, a complete worked example, the default-method helpers, and the bound-vs-controlled / stateless-helper-vs-Component trade-offs.
- [HTTP & files](docs/http-and-files.md): data & file *transfer* — a DI'd `HttpClient` (constructor-injected, `BaseAddress` at the app origin; fetch in `OnMountAsync` with cancel/retry/error handling), the typed file-picker input (`Input(Type: InputType.File, OnFiles:)` + `RaskFile` metadata; multipart on Server, JS chunked reads on WASM), and `Navigator.Download` (event-handler-only; served from `/_rask/download/…` on Server, base64 to JS on WASM).
- [Data access](docs/data-access.md): EF Core + SQLite, IDbContextFactory, loading in the lifecycle, vertical slices, DDD value objects, SQLite decimal gotcha.
- [SQLite production pragmas](docs/sqlite.md): the opt-in `Rask.SQLite` package — applies the Rails 8 production SQLite pragma set (journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, cache_size=2000 pages, mmap_size=128MiB, journal_size_limit=64MiB; temp_store opt-in) to every connection. Raw ADO.NET: `services.AddRaskSqlite(cs, configure?)` + inject `IRaskSqliteConnectionFactory`. Per-connection pragmas are re-applied on every pooled open (only journal_mode=WAL persists in the file); each option is overridable or nullable-to-skip via `SqlitePragmaOptions`. CONCURRENT WRITES: `factory.ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync(async (conn, ct) => …)` runs the work in a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and acquires the write lock through the raw sqlite3 handle with the native busy handler off — the only wait is an `await Task.Delay` at a CONSTANT 1ms fair interval (ported from rails/rails#51958; not exponential backoff) that FREES the thread (the .NET analog of Rails releasing the GVL); `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock up front, converting the otherwise UNRETRYABLE deferred read-then-write dead-lock into a plain waitable wait. Also `connection.BeginImmediate()` (returns a SqliteTransaction; its wait blocks the thread inside Microsoft.Data.Sqlite) and `connection.ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync(retry, work)`. `SqliteBusyRetryOptions` (Timeout=5s, PollInterval=1ms) via `AddRaskSqlite(cs, configure?, configureRetry?)`. Base package depends ONLY on Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and is reflection-free → works server-side, on MOBILE (Rask.Native, on-device — samples/Rask.Example.Native's Todos tab persists via SqliteTodoStore), and under trimming/AOT. NOT for the browser/WASM (single-threaded, WAL doesn't work, needs a native e_sqlite3 relink + manual whole-file persistence — the pragmas that justify this package don't apply there; use IIndexedDb/localStorage from Rask.Core.Browser, or the JS sqlite-wasm+OPFS stack for a real client-side DB; docs/sqlite.md#sqlite-in-the-browser-wasm). EF Core integration is a SEPARATE package `Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore`: `o.UseRaskSqlite(cs, configure?, configureRetry?)` (drop-in for UseSqlite; ConnectionOpened interceptor; pulls in Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite) — split out so the base stays EF-free for mobile/AOT. Passing configureRetry (even empty) registers a fair-interval `RaskSqliteExecutionStrategy` so SaveChanges/queries retry on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED (turns busy_timeout=0 and lowers Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's command timeout so the async strategy owns the wait; each EF command still routes through the driver's synchronous busy-retry so a contended attempt can block ~1s before the strategy takes over — the raw ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync path has no such floor; the implicit SaveChanges transaction stays DEFERRED — wrap a read-then-write txn in BeginImmediate). Backup companion `Rask.SQLite.Litestream` (docs/sqlite.md#continuous-backup-with-litestream): managed Litestream supervisor — `services.AddRaskSqliteLitestream(o => { o.DatabasePath; o.ReplicaUrl="s3://…"|"gcs://…"|"abs://…"|"file://…"; o.ConfigPath?; o.RestoreOnStartup=true; o.ShutdownGracePeriod=10s; })` registers a hosted BackgroundService that runs `litestream replicate` for the process lifetime (graceful SIGINT flush on shutdown), plus `await app.Services.RestoreSqliteFromLitestreamAsync()` to restore from the replica before opening the DB (no-op if the file exists). Runs the litestream binary via CliWrap (set ExecutablePath if not on PATH). Single-writer only; DB on local disk not a network share; ideal for ephemeral containers / Azure App Service Linux (DB on local disk, replicate to abs://, single instance, Always On). Backup failures log Critical, never crash the app. Snapshot companion `Rask.SQLite.Snapshots` (docs/sqlite.md#scheduled-snapshots): scheduled CONSISTENT full-file backups via SQLite Online Backup API (`SqliteConnection.BackupDatabase`) — NO external binary, works on minimal/distroless + Alpine images. `services.AddRaskSqliteSnapshots(o => { DatabasePath; DestinationDirectory; Interval=6h; Retain=7; SnapshotOnStartup=false; BusyTimeout=30s; })` runs a hosted BackgroundService (PeriodicTimer) that snapshots + prunes to newest N; or inject `ISqliteSnapshotter` for on-demand `SnapshotAsync()`. Swap the `ISqliteSnapshotStore` (default DirectorySnapshotStore) for object storage. Complements Litestream (streaming) or stands alone. Docker: mount a volume for DestinationDirectory or snapshots are lost on container removal; DB on local/named-volume not NFS/CIFS (WAL locking).
- [CQRS](docs/cqrs.md): the opt-in, standalone `Rask.Cqrs` package — a source-generated, reflection-free CQRS/mediator. IQuery<T>/ICommand/ICommand<T>/INotification + their handlers, dispatched via a single IDispatcher — DispatchAsync (one method for queries and commands, response type inferred) and PublishAsync for notifications; register with AddRaskCqrs(). Handlers are wired by a Roslyn generator (no runtime reflection, no assembly scanning, [DynamicDependency]-preserved ctors) so it publishes clean under the WASM/AOT trimmer. Pipeline behaviors (IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResult>, registered via AddOpenBehavior / AddBehavior) are the decorator hook for logging/validation/etc; none ship. Notifications fan out Sequential or WhenAll. Diagnostics RASK028 (ambiguous handler) / RASK029 (unregisterable handler). Depends only on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions.
- [Browser APIs](docs/browser-apis.md): the map of all typed Web-API wrappers (46) — shared vs WASM-only, one-shot vs subscription, with the inject-from-ctor pattern and the push/[JSInvokable] mechanism.
- [JS interop](docs/js-interop.md): scoped CSS/JS, element refs, IJSRuntime, typed browser APIs — shared (both transports) in Rask.Core.Browser ( plus the PWA APIs IWebPush/INotifications/IBadge/IWakeLock, and the all-host headless Shareable — OS share sheet, attaches data-rask-share to your element and fires navigator.share in the click gesture so it works on Server too, native-upgraded in the shell; plus the all-host GestureTrigger family — FullscreenTrigger/ScreenOrientationTrigger/EyeDropperTrigger/InstallTrigger/MediaCaptureTrigger/PictureInPictureTrigger, headless data-rask-gesture components that run activation-gated WASM-only APIs inside the click gesture so they reach the Server host declaratively); imperative in-process WASM+Native-shared in Rask.Client.Browser (IShare — code-driven share, native head backend on Native); WASM-only in Rask.Wasm.Browser (IScreenOrientation/IFullscreen/IInstallPrompt + device APIs ISerial/IUsb/IHid/IBluetooth/IMediaDevices/IEyeDropper/IPictureInPicture/IIdleDetector).
- [AOT compilation](docs/aot.md): opt-in full WASM AOT via `-p:RaskWasmAot=true` (default keeps the Mono interpreter; needs the wasm-tools workload). A reflection-free `TypedParserRegistry` seeds every BCL `IParsable` primitive and resolves route/query/form string values with no runtime generics; the RoutesGenerator auto-registers custom `IParsable` route/query param types; `RaskBinding.RegisterParsable<T>()` registers custom form-model value types; `InvokeAsync<T>` needs a `JsonSerializerContext` for custom T. Runtime builds under `IsAotCompatible` and the WASM sample under `EnableAotAnalyzer`, so every warnings-as-errors build enforces AOT-safety; the full AOT publish runs nightly. Mono WASM AOT is mixed-mode (interpreter stays), so the win is a clean bundle + faster binding, not crash-avoidance.
- [Data layer](docs/data.md): the opt-in `Rask.Data` package — a provider-agnostic DDD base for EF Core apps. `AggregateRoot<TId>` (Id + CreatedAt/UpdatedAt audit stamps + a domain-events buffer via Raise/DomainEvents/ClearDomainEvents), opt-in marker interfaces ISoftDeletable (adds DeletedAt) / IVersioned (adds an int concurrency token), and three ISaveChangesInterceptors: AuditingInterceptor (stamps timestamps, bumps Version), SoftDeleteInterceptor (rewrites a Deleted ISoftDeletable to Modified + sets DeletedAt so db.Remove soft-deletes; global query filter DeletedAt==null hides it — use IgnoreQueryFilters() to see/restore), DomainEventInterceptor (after commit, publishes each aggregate's INotification events via Rask.Cqrs IDispatcher.PublishAsync in a fresh scope, then clears — set RaskDataOptions.DispatchDomainEventsInProcess=false when an outbox owns delivery). Wire with services.AddRaskData() (registers the interceptors + a TimeProvider) + o.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>()) on the DbContext + modelBuilder.ApplyRaskConventions() in OnModelCreating (adds the query filter + IsConcurrencyToken). Optimistic concurrency: round-trip the original Version (hidden form field) and set Entry(x).Property(e=>e.Version).OriginalValue before SaveChanges → DbUpdateConcurrencyException on a stale save. Depends on Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore + Rask.Cqrs; server-side (not WASM). The base the `rask generate feature` --soft-delete/--concurrency/--events scaffolder output builds on.
- [Transactional outbox](docs/outbox.md): the opt-in `Rask.Outbox` package — durable, crash-safe domain-event delivery on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis), the durable counterpart to Rask.Data's in-process publisher. Mark an event `IOutboxEvent` (: INotification); the `OutboxInterceptor` (SavingChanges) drains each tracked aggregate's IOutboxEvent domain events into `OutboxMessage` rows on the SAME context/transaction (atomic — never written for a rolled-back change), and the hosted `OutboxProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) publishes the oldest unprocessed batch via IDispatcher.PublishAsync and stamps ProcessedAt (or Attempts++/Error, retry to MaxAttempts) — at-least-once. A source generator registers each IOutboxEvent type (name→Type) at module load so the drain deserializes with no runtime Type.GetType/scanning. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskData(o => o.DispatchDomainEventsInProcess = false)` (outbox owns delivery — avoid double-dispatch) + `services.AddRaskOutbox<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval=5s; BatchSize=100; MaxAttempts=10; })` + `.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>())` on the context + `modelBuilder.AddRaskOutbox()` in OnModelCreating (maps OutboxMessage). Same INotificationHandler<T> reacts whether delivered in-process or via the outbox. Server-side; SQLite is single-writer so it polls (no SKIP LOCKED), WAL+busy_timeout keep reads flowing; one processor per app; add an EF migration for the table. `rask generate feature --outbox` emits it.
- [Background jobs](docs/jobs.md): the opt-in `Rask.Jobs` package — durable background work on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). A job is a `IJob` (: Rask.Cqrs ICommand) run off the request thread by an ordinary `ICommandHandler<TJob>`. Inject `IJobQueue` and `EnqueueAsync(job)` (run asap) / `ScheduleAsync(job, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `Job` row (Type name + JSON payload + RunAt) via IDbContextFactory (its OWN transaction — not atomic with a business change; use Rask.Outbox for that). The hosted `JobProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due jobs (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), dispatches each via IDispatcher.DispatchAsync((ICommand)job) in a fresh scope, stamps ProcessedAt; on failure Attempts++/Error and pushes RunAt out by exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped at MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 25) → then a dead letter kept for inspection; completed jobs purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d, Zero=keep). Durable interval-recurring: `o.AddRecurring<T>(name, every, factory)` enqueues a fresh job per interval, tracked in a RecurringJobState table so a restart never double-runs it (single catch-up if overdue). A source generator registers each IJob type (name→Type) at module load for reflection-free rehydration. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskJobs<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval; MaxAttempts; AddRecurring(...); })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskJobs()` in OnModelCreating (maps Job + RecurringJobState) + `rask db add AddJobs && rask db update`. Server-side; one processor per app. `rask generate job <Name>` (alias `g j`) scaffolds the IJob record + handler.
- [Mobile & PWA](docs/pwa.md): build installable mobile apps in C#. WASM = full PWA (install, true offline, push, every device API). Server = installable + push-capable via AddRaskPwa (serves manifest + service worker, auto-registers it, emits the manifest link into the server-rendered head), but NOT an offline app (offline navigations show a static offline.html; no background sync; install-prompt + activation-bound device APIs stay WASM-only). Typed Web app manifest (WebAppManifest in Rask.Core.Browser; WASM UsePwa / Server AddRaskPwa), default service worker (rask-sw.js; shared push/notificationclick handlers in Rask.Core), IWebPush + INotifications + IBadge + IWakeLock (Rask.Core.Browser, both hosts), `rask new MyApp --template wasm --pwa` / `rask new MyApp --pwa`. Sending push from the backend: the opt-in `Rask.WebPush` package (IWebPushSender, VAPID RFC 8292 + aes128gcm RFC 8291, zero external deps).
- [Native mobile (iOS/Android)](docs/native.md): the `Rask.Native` WebView-hybrid host — run a Rask app natively on iOS/Android inside a platform WebView, driven by the SAME render/diff pipeline as Server/WASM (it subclasses LiveSessionBase). Two modes: Native+Local (in-process, offline — `NativeAppHost.RunLocalAsync<App>`) and Native+Server (thin native shell over a remote Rask Server — `ConnectToServer`). The platform WebView is abstracted behind the `INativeWebView` bridge (WKWebView on iOS / android.webkit.WebView on Android), implemented in the app head, so the library builds/unit-tests on plain net10.0 with no iOS/Android workloads. Ships the native client dialect (rask.native.js) + boot shell. Scaffold + run: `rask new MyApp --template native`, then `dotnet workload install ios android` and `dotnet build -t:Run -f net10.0-android` (or `-f net10.0-ios`). The `rask-native` template (shared components + Platforms/iOS WKWebView head + Platforms/Android WebView head) ships and runs end-to-end on both platforms; the template's App.cs pads Body by `env(safe-area-inset-*)` (with a viewport-fit=cover viewport) so content clears the notch/status bar. The native client shares the transport-neutral DOM helpers (rAF input/scroll coalescing, keyboard + drag, scoped-CSS FOUC gating) with the Server/WASM clients via common spliced modules (rask-input.js/rask-scoped.js/rask-events.js). The RUNNABLE native showcase is two examples mirroring the Server/WASM pairing, both mounting the SAME Rask.Example.Shared.App: `samples/Rask.Example.Native` (Native + Local, in-process — the peer of the WASM sample) and `samples/Rask.Example.Native.Server` (Native + Server, a thin shell over a remote Rask.Example.Server — the peer of the Server sample). Both multi-target net10.0-ios;net10.0-android, so they sit OUTSIDE Rask.slnx and are compile-gated by a dedicated macOS `native` CI job across every project × TFM; `-t:Run -f net10.0-android|net10.0-ios`. On-device E2E is Appium (tests/Rask.Native.Appium.Tests): Appium installs + drives the REAL app on an Android emulator / iOS simulator, switches into the WebView, and asserts the showcase rendered with scoped CSS + Bootstrap (served through NativeOriginAssets) — run in the macOS `native-appium` CI job (boots the emulator, `appium --allow-insecure=uiautomator2:chromedriver_autodownload`, EmbedAssembliesIntoApk APK). This replaced the old Playwright-in-Chromium headless shim (which masked a real device-only bug: the boot shell loads at /index.native.html, a path NativeOriginAssets now serves). To serve a FULL app's assets on-device (not just the two boot files), Rask.Native provides `NativeOriginAssets.Resolve(path, readStaticFile)` (the origin request table: boot shell + client, scoped /_rask/a/* from ScopedAssetRegistry, and your wwwroot/Bootstrap/data via a caller-supplied bundled-asset reader — Android AssetManager / iOS NSBundle) + `NativeAssetHttpHandler` (serves the in-process demo HttpClient from the same table so data/*.json works offline). Native header & footer: a native page is a COMPOSED tree — the native bars (`NativeHeaderBar`/`NativeTabBar`/`NativeToolbar`) as siblings of a `NativeWebView` that hosts the ordinary page shell (Doctype/Html/Head/Body). They are ordinary factory-built components in `Rask.Native.Components` (all inherit `NativeComponent : Component`, composed in `Render()`, NOT base-class slots), with type-safe `NativeIcon` SF-Symbol/drawable pairs + `Features.Routes.*` tabs. The platform head implements `INativeChrome` (registered like `IShare`, assign `webView.ChromeView`) and projects the bars to a real UINavigationBar+UITabBar/UIToolbar (iOS) / top+bottom bars (Android), serializing the NativeWebView's HTML into the WebView between them. Bars render NO HTML — nesting one inside the HTML (an element child, or inside NativeWebView content) is a RASK032 compile error; bars are collected during the render walk (DI-correct, last of a kind wins), pushed with a byte noop-guard, button taps run OnClick + tabs navigate. Style the bars with `NativeColor` (the color sibling of NativeIcon: Hex/Rgba/Adaptive(light,dark)/System) — per-bar `Background`/`Tint`/`TitleColor` (+ tab-bar `UnselectedTint`) or an app-wide `NativeTheme` on host.Services; per-bar wins, then theme, then the platform default (unset keeps the OS look; adaptive colors track dark mode). The Android head resolves each NativeIcon drawable so tabs/buttons show real icons. NativeTab takes an optional `Badge` string (unread count) → UITabBarItem.BadgeValue (iOS) / icon overlay (Android); bind it to live state and it updates on the next render. NativeHeaderBar takes optional `Segments` (2–3 labels, shown in place of the title) → UISegmentedControl titleView (iOS) / button row (Android), controlled via `SelectedSegment` + `OnSegmentChanged(int)` (reuses nativeTap dispatch). A `NativeMenuButton` bar item (with `NativeMenuItem` entries: Title/Icon/OnClick/Destructive) opens a native overflow pull-down → UIMenu (iOS) / PopupMenu (Android), reusing nativeTap dispatch. A `NativeBackButton` (header Leading) pops WebView history like hardware Back (the initial render replaces the boot shell URL in history so Back lands on the app's first screen). Sharing an app web+native? Branch on the host via `IsNative`/`IsServer`/`IsWasm`/`IsIOS`/`IsAndroid` (+ the `HostShell`/`HostEngine`/`HostPlatform` enums, three orthogonal render-cache-safe axes): compose the native tree under `IsNative`, render a web `BsNavbar` on Server/WASM. Preview / pre-1.0: native device backends (native push/biometrics) are the main remaining follow-up (the scoped-JS invoke gate + file uploads also stay host-specific for now). WebView hybrid (C# runs native, view is a WebView) — HTML in a WebView plus the one bounded native header/footer surface, not a general native-control renderer.
- [Authentication](docs/authentication.md): cookie/JWT, Authorize, route guards.
- [Observability](docs/observability.md): structured logging, the `Rask.Server` meter + activity source, `AddRaskLiveSessions()` health check.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): `RaskLiveOptions` (shared: diff mode, path base, session cap) + `RaskServerOptions` (server-only WS/grace/idle/backpressure limits) + `RaskUploadOptions` (upload size + per-session quota), appsettings binding + startup validation.
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): containerizing the apps — opt-in `--docker` on the three web templates scaffolds a production multi-stage Dockerfile (+ `.dockerignore`): `rask-server` and `rask-wasm-hosted` build on the .NET SDK image and run on `aspnet:10.0` (non-root, port 8080, `UseHttpsRedirection` no-ops in-container so terminate TLS at the proxy and forward the WebSocket upgrade); the standalone `rask-wasm` bundle publishes then serves from `nginx:alpine` with a bundled `nginx.conf` (SPA `try_files` fallback, `application/wasm` MIME, `gzip_static` for the baked `*.gz`). `rask-native` is a mobile app (app-store package, not a container). GitHub Pages / sub-path via `/p:RaskPathBase=`. One-command deploy of that Dockerfile: `rask deploy --host user@box [--domain app.example.com]` builds the image on the box over SSH and runs it — with `--domain` a shared Caddy proxy adds automatic HTTPS and deploys are zero-downtime (blue-green), multiple apps to one host.
- [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): ARIA via the `Aria` dictionary, `Role`/`TabIndex`, the `Img` alt-text analyzer (RASK023), and automatic navigation a11y on the Server host (SPA route changes show a progress bar, move focus into the new page's `<main>`, and announce the route via `aria-live`).
- [Migration from Blazor](docs/migration-from-blazor.md): mapping Blazor concepts to Rask.
- [Diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md): RASK001–031 compile-time diagnostics + fixes, including IDE quick-fixes (lightbulb) for RASK001 (add `required`) and RASK023 (insert `Alt: ""`), shipped in `Rask.Generators.CodeFixes`.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): the `Rask.Testing` package (`RaskTest.Render(component)` → `RenderedComponent`; `.ClickAsync()`/`.InvokeAsync(handlerId, json?)` dispatch handlers + re-render; `.Html`/`.HandlerId`/`.Attr` query) for in-process component unit tests, plus Playwright E2E patterns.

## Contributing to Rask itself
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repo conventions for AI assistants + the `.claude/skills/` workflows.
- [Development workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): the format → warnings-as-errors → tests →
  benchmarks → docs → review → PR gate, CI, nightly, analyzers.
- [Code analysis](docs/code-analysis.md): analyzers and adoption.
